newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Britain says would like Fiji back in Commonwealth.
newsitem.headline: Britain says would like Fiji back in Commonwealth.

text.p: Britain has welcomed an initial step by Fiji to scrap its racially-biased constitution and said it would like the South Pacific nation to return to the Commonwealth from which it was expelled in 1990.
"We would like to see Fiji return. But this is not a decision which the U.K. (United Kingdom) alone can take," said British junior Foreign Office minister Jeremy Hanley.
"However, early progress towards a constitutional settlement should help achieve this goal," Hanley said in a statement received here on Thursday.
Speaking to Fijian reporters in Suva on Tuesday, Hanley said he had delivered a letter from British Prime Minister John Major to his Fijian counterpart, Sitiveni Rabuka, welcoming the review.
An independent review of Fiji's constitution tabled in parliament on Tuesday called for an end to the political dominance of indigenous Fijians.
Under the current constitution, indigenous Fijians are guaranteed a majority in parliament under a voting system which bars ethnic Indians from contesting certain seats.
The constitutinal review has so far gained widespread support in Fiji from both indigenous Fijians and ethnic Indians.
It will go before a joint parliamentary committee for discussion. Any constitutional changes must be approved by at least two-thirds of parliament.
Rabuka staged a 1987 coup as commander of the armed forces, arguing indigenous Fijians were losing control of their country where Indians make up 45 percent of the population.

In 1990 Rabuka introduced the racially-biased constitution, resulting in Fiji's expulsion from the Commonwealth. India opposes Fiji's rentry into the Commonwealth as long as it maintains its racially-biased constitution.
Hanley said Fiji would gain much economically by settling the constitution issue with consensus.
"The right decisions now can lead to a brighter future for all...Your diversity can be strength," said Hanley, who was in the South Pacific for talks with island leaders.
"One of the main foundation stones to stability, investor confidence and prosperity will be a return to the Commonwealth."
The Commonwealth is a voluntary association of Britain and its former dependencies.
